text: Cost and latency are almost always working exactly as designed, and they still need watching — 'as designed' at ten times last month's traffic can mean a bill that triples and a product that suddenly feels slow.
A single running total isn't enough to act on. A real dashboard breaks requests, cost, and latency out over time and by model and country, so a spike is traceable to a cause.

A single call's cost and latency are rarely the number that matters. A multi-step agent session can rack up a dozen calls before it returns an answer — looking at the whole session is where the real expense shows up.
One lever that moves both numbers at once: caching. A repeated or near-identical prompt served from cache skips the model call entirely — cost and latency drop to nearly zero on that repeat.
The other lever is knowing what each model actually costs. Per-million-token prices can differ five to ten times between a frontier model and a smaller one doing the same job.
Cost and latency scale with every token in and out, often without anyone changing a line of code. Next up: drift — what happens when the inputs themselves start to change.
